summary: @hubsync/web-sdk-react preinstall downloads Bun runtime and executes obfuscated sibling payload
details: package.json declares scripts.preinstall = 'node setup.mjs'. setup.mjs is itself obfuscated (hex-named identifiers, wrapped call helpers) and, when Bun is absent from PATH, downloads a Bun release zip from github.com/oven-sh/bun for the detected platform/arch, extracts the bun/bun.exe binary to a temp dir, chmod 0755's it, and execFileSync's it against the sibling file math_init.js. math_init.js is a 727 KB file whose entire body is a hex-named string-array-shuffle obfuscator output (rotator WV8StW, decoder hc1jfK9 with a custom alphabet, ~1000-entry constant table) with no comments or readable identifiers. Executing an opaque obfuscated payload under an alternate runtime at npm-install time is a fetch-and-execute pattern that hands the shipped bytes arbitrary execution on the installer's host and is structured to bypass Node-focused supply-chain scanners. The package.json name is @hubsync/web-sdk-react while the description is 'Verdocs Web SDK for React' and dist/ code references api.verdocs.com and beta.verdocs.com, so the package presents as the legitimate Verdocs SDK under an unrelated scope while adding install-time execution machinery not present in the upstream project.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
